subject: Re: AWS private offer — pricing, term split and approver lag
messages:
From: Sara Holden <sara.holden@edgeworks.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgeworks.com
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer question — can we shorten term and keep price?

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile. Procurement at EdgeWorks is pushing back on a two-year committed term in the private offer. Darren (CFO) is open to a 12-months commitment but wants the same unit pricing you quoted for two years.

Two quick asks:
- Is there a structuring option where we keep the quoted unit price but split the commitment across 12 months + a small usage buffer?
- If we reduce the term, what internal approvals (buyer/CFO/legal) will be required on your side and how long does activation take once signed?

I can loop in procurement contacts if that helps. Also attaching the procurement template they prefer (proc template referenced).

Thanks —
Sara
Senior Procurement Manager
EdgeWorks LLC

Attachment: procurement_template_edgeworks.docx (docx)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sara Holden <sara.holden@edgeworks.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — can we shorten term and keep price?

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for raising Darren's preference. Short answer: yes, there are two viable paths but they come with tradeoffs. High-level options below; see attached XLS for numbers.

Option A — 12-months + usage buffer (recommended for procurement velocity)
- Keep unit price at quoted level if EdgeWorks commits to an annualized ARR floor equal to the two-year price (we model the two-year spread into a 12-month equivalent).
- Add a 10% usage buffer that rolls into the next month if unused (reduces spike risk).
- Requires CFO (Darren) sign-off and Legal acceptance of a short addendum — internal activation SLA: 3 business days after countersignature.

Option B — 12-months with smaller discount (quicker approvals)
- Reduce unit discount by ~8% relative to the 2-year quote.
- Can be executed with standard PO + procurement approval without direct CFO sign-off on our side; activation SLA: 2 business days after PO + standard verification.

Internal approvals and gating (our side):
- Sales owner (me) + Sales Ops approval (Jasmine) for price exceptions >5%.
- Finance needs to approve any term/price restructuring that changes billing cadence (Ben is on copy).
- Legal review for addendum language if you want the exact two-year economic replicated over 12 months.

I attached the pricing workbook and a draft addendum. Next steps I suggest: you confirm which option the buyer prefers and we can coordinate a short CFO-to-CFO note or handle via procurement/P.O.

—Markus
Head of Marketplace Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-pricing-options-v3.xlsx (xlsx), draft-private-offer.docx (docx)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer question — pricing/term options (internal)

Markus / Ben — forwarding Sara's note + our pricing proposals. Quick internal checklist before we reply to EdgeWorks: 

1) Confirm finance tolerance for matching 2yr economics over 12 months (Ben) — will this create revenue recognition or billing complexity we need to flag?
2) Legal redline needed only if they want the addendum replicating 2yr economics (I can scope a 1-pager addendum template).
3) If Option A, confirm activation SLA and any operational pre-reqs (accounts provisioning, billing mapping).

Ben — can you run a quick sensitivity on ARR leakage vs. payment schedule? If we accept Option A we need to be explicit on clawback or shortfall mechanism.

On the procurement timeline: procurement team at EdgeWorks tends to do a single PO and then issue payment net30; if we need CFO-to-CFO note we should prepare a one-paragraph exec summary.

Jasmine
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the clear options. Darren prefers Option A (12-month commitment with the two-year economic) provided we get the short addendum that documents the ARR floor and a shortfall clause. Procurement will issue a PO after we receive the addendum + evidence pack for SOC2 and data handling (their compliance team asked for these).

Practical items from our side:
- Please upload the evidence pack (SOC2 report, data-retention policy, subprocessor list) to the DocuSign envelope or share a secure link.
- We will route the PO to Finance; expect a 48–72 hour procurement processing window after we have the addendum and evidence.

If you can get the addendum and the evidence pack in the next 24 hours we can aim to have a PO out to you by Monday.

Best,
